notes: DRAFT from the Monster Classification & Guild System bible v1.0 (user PDF), sections 8 and 9. 30 guilds, an 8-step membership ladder, per-guild reputation and facilities. Not yet wired to quests or the HUD; see 13_Production/monster_guild_integration.md for what needs the user OK. The player cannot own a guild (Canon section 4). The Adventurers Consortium is the existing Adventurers Guild and keeps the F to SSS rank ladder.

rules: Track reputation per guild, not as one global value.
Positive: completed contracts, donations, discoveries, rescues, fair conduct.
Negative: abandoning missions, stealing guild property, harming protected creatures, breaking contracts, betraying members.
High reputation unlocks discounts, rare recipes, restricted quests, mentors, titles and an advisory say in guild votes.
A player may be respected by one guild and distrusted by another; multiple compatible memberships are allowed.

memberLadder.name: Applicant
memberLadder.exampleRequirements: Registration, identity check or introductory task.

memberLadder.name: Initiate
memberLadder.exampleRequirements: Basic test, first contribution or recommendation.

memberLadder.name: Member
memberLadder.exampleRequirements: Completed starter quest and code acceptance.

memberLadder.name: Expert
memberLadder.access: High-risk quests, mentorship and restricted facilities.

memberLadder.name: Officer
memberLadder.access: Team leadership and quest recommendations (honorary standing; no guild property).
memberLadder.exampleRequirements: Trust, leadership record, guild vote or appointment.

memberLadder.name: Master
memberLadder.access: Rare services and teaching rights (honorary; the player never runs a guild).

memberLadder.name: Grandmaster
memberLadder.access: Guild-wide influence and unique story access.
memberLadder.exampleRequirements: Major narrative achievement; usually one or few.

standings.note: Below distrustedBelow the guild refuses services and contracts; below bannedBelow membership is revoked and tier resets. Standing recovers only by completing guild contracts or donations.

reputationEvents.text: A donation to the guild (per 100 copper).
A discovery the guild cares about.

facilities: Hall and reception: membership, noticeboards, contracts and public services.
Training yard: combat practice, sparring, skill trials and weapon instruction.
Library or archive: maps, monster records, spell research and lore.
Workshop: crafting, repairs, enchanting and alchemy.
Infirmary: healing, recovery and status-effect treatment.
Stable, docks or hangar: mounts and transport where appropriate.
Vault and auction room: escrow, rare goods, guild funds and secure storage.
Private rooms: party planning, guild meetings, faction story scenes.

rivalries.text: Cooperate on contracts; compete for high-profile targets.
Cooperate on caravan security; dispute reward pricing.
Share research; compete over patents and rare catalysts.
Cooperate on rescue; disagree over capture and ownership.
Ideological conflict and occasional joint containment operations.
Cooperate on translation; dispute ownership and access.
Share information but compete for influence.

councilNote: The Free Cities Guild Council can mediate charters, monopolies, sanctions and inter-city conflicts.
